data.claim: A failing test id that also fails on the base is always attributed as baseline-red (still_failing) because the comparison uses the id's presence in the base's failing list only, never its failure text; a branch that clears or adds an offender inside an already-red test is hidden.
data.falsifier: If the id-only comparison suffices, a test red on the base with a DIFFERENT failure text on the branch still records partial baseline-red; if a new offender must read as FAILED/new, the text has to be compared.
data.mechanism: services/gates/baseline_red.py _verdicts/_tally decide still-failing by 'i in failing' (id membership); the failure text (failed_reasons) is discarded, so an id the base also fails keeps reading baseline-red when the branch changed its assertion output.
data.probe: test_a_new_offender_in_an_already_red_test_is_new_not_baseline_red (tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py): run it on the fix -- gate stays 'failed' and names the id a new failure -- and run it on the unfixed code -- gate records 'partial' baseline-red.
data.probe_output: Fixed code: test passes; 6 pre-existing red tests attributed baseline-red (still_failing). Unfixed code: found['different'] absent, still_failing==[id], red==True.
data.question: Does ddflow baseline-red compare only failing test ids, so a new offender in a test already red on the base goes unseen?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED (R10081c55f6): baseline-red compared failing test ids only; the fix compares failure text too. Probe test_a_new_offender_in_an_already_red_test_is_new_not_baseline_red passes on the fix (gate failed, new_failures/different named) and would fail on the id-only code (still_failing, red).

chunk_findings.detail: `outcomes, cmds, seen, base_sigs = ran` now unpacks four values, but this diff does not change `_run_chunks`; the old code unpacked exactly three values (`outcomes, cmds, seen = ran`). On any call with at least one uncached id, `_run_chunks` still returns a 3-tuple, so `on_base` raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack` before returning a result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:107

chunk_findings.detail: The cached path returns `_tally(ids, known, before)` without any base failure signatures. Since `known` is a `dict[str, bool]`, `_tally` receives `onbase=None`, so `_differs` always returns `False` for cached ids. The original bug therefore remains on cache hits: with `ids=["test_x"]`, `known={"test_x": True}`, `before={"test_x": "new assertion"}`, and the base actually failing `test_x` with `"old assertion"`, `on_base` returns `red=True, different=[]` and hides the new offender.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:103

chunk_findings.detail: `_run_chunks` now collects and returns `base_sigs`, but the cache write on the next line still stores only `seen`: `cache_store(repo, sha, seen, ttl_s, gdef.command)`. On a warm cache for the same base SHA and command, the cached base result has no failure text for already-failing ids. A later branch with a new offender in an already-red test then cannot compare the branch failure text against the base text, so the fix stops working after the first run populates the cache. This is an environment-dependent failure: the same inputs produce different gate results depending on whether the base result was just run or served from cache.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_run_chunks

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_new_offender_in_an_already_red_test_is_new_not_baseline_red` builds `cfg.gates` with only `baseline_cache_ttl_s` and `baseline_red_auto`. For the `unit_tests` gate, `GB.apply` needs `unit_tests_max_files`, `unit_tests_hub_importers`, `unit_tests_max_hops`, and `unit_tests_name_max_tests` to decide whether the failing `ID` is within the measurable file budget; the sibling test at line ~503 supplies these for the same `ID`, but this test omits them. With this `cfg`, `GB.apply` will raise `AttributeError` for the missing attribute or classify `ID` as unmeasured (the same `ID` is the suite’s unmeasured example at line 442), so the regression test fails before exercising the new baseline-text comparison.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py:459

chunk_findings.detail: `changed = list(found.get("different") or (()))` treats a missing or empty `different` as the one-element tuple `((),)`, so `list(...)` is `[()]`, which is truthy. Any branch that already has a real new id (`fresh` non-empty) and no signature diff therefore enters the note and dies in `', '.join(changed[:BR.SHOWN])` with `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, tuple found`. Given `found = {"still_failing": ["old_test"], "different": []}` and `ids = ["old_test", "brand_new"]`, the gate should report `brand_new` as a new failure; it raises instead. `or ()` would have been the empty sequence; `or (())` is not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:88

chunk_findings.detail: A full cache hit never compares failure text, so the bug returns inside the TTL. `on_base` calls `_tally(ids, known, before)` with no `onbase` when every id is already in `known`, and `_run_chunks` still does `cache_store(..., seen, ...)` with only `{id: bool}`. Given `ttl_s > 0`, ids already cached as failing, and `before={"tests/test_arch_interfaces.py::test_real_tree_ratchet_against_committed_baseline": "<new offender>"}`, `_differs` sees no base signature (`if not base: return False`), so `still` covers every id and `red` is True. The new offender is hidden again, which is the ratchet this change is meant to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_tally

chunk_findings.detail: When a test id appears in `found["different"]` and is not in `found["still_failing"]`, it is not added to `known`, so it lands in `fresh`. The function then returns a message that says that test is a “new failure(s) not failing on {base}”, and also sets `found["new_failures"]` to include it, even though the appended note says the same id “failed on {base} too, but differently”. For example, with `ids=["test_x"]` and `found={"red": True, "different": ["test_x"], "still_failing": [], "unmeasured": []}`, this incorrectly records and reports `test_x` as not failing on the base while simultaneously stating it did fail on the base. The different offender should be reported separately and not placed in `new_failures` as a base-clean failure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:89-101

chunk_findings.detail: The new `outcomes, cmds, seen, base_sigs = ran` unpacking assumes `_run_chunks` now returns four values, but `_run_chunks` is not changed in this diff and the removed line unpacked only `(outcomes, cmds, seen)`. Any non-cached run reaches this line and raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 4, got 3)`, so the gate crashes instead of returning a baseline verdict.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: When all requested ids are already cached (`todo` is empty), the function returns `_tally(ids, known, before)` without `onbase`; `_differs` sees no base text and returns `False` for every id. Example: `ids=["test_arch_interfaces.py::test_real_tree_ratchet_against_committed_baseline"]`, `known={"test_arch_interfaces.py::test_real_tree_ratchet_against_committed_baseline": True}` from the base cache, and `before={"test_arch_interfaces.py::test_real_tree_ratchet_against_committed_baseline": "program git ..."}`. The result is `red=True` with `different=[]`, so the new offender in an already-red cached base test is still classified as baseline-red—the exact bug this change is meant to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base cached path

chunk_findings.detail: `_run_chunks` now computes and returns `base_sigs`, but the cache write is still only `cache_store(repo, sha, seen, ttl_s, gdef.command)`. A base-failing id that is already cached as `True` is later reused without any corresponding entry in `base_sigs`. In the bug’s own scenario, the already-red test on main is exactly the kind of status that is cached; on a second gate run for the same base sha, the branch failure text for that cached id has no base text to compare against, so the new `_differs` logic cannot tell a same-text baseline failure from a new offender. The cache entry needs to persist the base failure signature for `base_sigs` to survive cache hits.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_run_chunks

chunk_findings.detail: This test builds `cfg = SimpleNamespace(gates=SimpleNamespace(baseline_cache_ttl_s=0, baseline_red_auto="on"))` and then calls `GB.apply` for a `unit_tests` gate. The paired test in the same change supplies `unit_tests_max_files`, `unit_tests_hub_importers`, `unit_tests_max_hops`, and `unit_tests_name_max_tests`, which the `unit_tests` gate-baseline path reads from `cfg.gates`. Running this test will fail with `AttributeError` (or otherwise take a disabled/zero-config path) before reaching the regression assertions, so the test does not exercise the intended behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py:test_a_new_offender_in_an_already_red_test_is_new_not_baseline_red

chunk_findings.detail: `changed = list(found.get("different") or (()))` treats a missing or empty `different` as the tuple `((),)`, so `changed` becomes `[()]`, which is truthy. The common case is a new failing id with no signature diffs (`found["different"]` absent or `[]`) and a non-empty `fresh`: the `if fresh` / `if changed` branch then does `", ".join(changed[:BR.SHOWN])` and raises `TypeError` (sequence item 0 is a tuple, not a str), so the gate crashes instead of reporting the new failure. `or ()` was intended; `(())` is a one-element tuple.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:88

chunk_findings.detail: The new signature compare is thrown away as soon as the base sha is cached. `_run_chunks` still does `cache_store(repo, sha, seen, ttl_s, gdef.command)` with only `{id: bool}`, and the `not todo` path calls `_tally(ids, known, before)` with no `onbase`. `_differs` then returns False whenever base text is missing, so those ids land in `still_failing`. Given `ttl_s > 0`, the same failing id, and `before` text that differs from the base: the first call can correctly set `red` False, but the next call on that sha hits `cached: True` and reports `red` True again, which is the bug this change claims to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_run_chunks
